prose_updates.tldr: For the exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue of GENE Equation (6), a primitive edgewise inequality on support-closed matching-component additive-noise models forces a positive reversal-correcting insertion at every wrong order, so best improvement and independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. This is a certified success region, not a theorem for Li et al.'s full nonlinear class. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), an explicitly parameterized relatively open bivariate family, including a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily, makes the identifiable causal model \(X\to Y\) have the wrong order as its unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer with score advantage strictly greater than \(\eta\); the universal sharp supremum is \(1/2\). Cross-fitted simultaneous bands abstain at unresolved independence labels; on separated labels, \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\), and direct margin inequalities yield the sufficient sample size \(n\gtrsim\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\), with the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\) and no minimax claim. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the stated HSIC separation promise, the set-valued output covers \(G_0\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) even when the width inequalities fail; those inequalities are required only for singleton recovery, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The success certificate is sufficient only on matching-component DAGs and is not an observable necessary-and-sufficient boundary for general GENE landscapes. The sharp bivariate construction proves a margin-indexed relatively open failure region, including a relatively open non-affine subfamily, inside the identifiable nonlinear-ANM class and attains the universal one-half supremum only as a limit; it does not classify the intervening general class. Exact independence remains discontinuous: the population trap handles it pointwise by support geometry throughout its open structural family, while finite-sample inference requires the stated HSIC separation promise and otherwise retains both labels. Under the matching class and that separation promise, simultaneous coverage still gives \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) when the score and HSIC width inequalities fail, but only the width inequalities certify singleton recovery; the compatible-DAG union may then be singleton or multiple. The residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC radius uses the stated nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The displayed sample-size order suppresses fixed regularity constants and is sufficient, not minimax optimal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered population results are a compact-support identification bridge, a matching-subclass insertion-navigation theorem, a six-node strict separation witness, finite-query oracle recovery, a quadratic positive-gain witness, and, for every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), a sharp relatively open bivariate trapped-order family with a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily. The wrong order is the unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer by more than \(\eta\), while the universal supremum of this score advantage is \(1/2\). The matching-subclass theorem does not establish success on Li et al.'s full nonlinear class; the nonlinear witnesses transfer to that class only existentially, and the trap does not contradict Theorem 4.3 because its global-ranking premise fails there. The simultaneous-band theorem gives \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\) on separated labels when \(w_R<\underline v/2\), together with direct sufficient conditions \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the existing HSIC separation promise, \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) remains valid even when those width inequalities fail; singleton recovery requires the inequalities, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple. No minimax rate, observable general-class boundary, or claim against Li et al. Theorem 4.3 is made. The released Sachs workflow remains an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold does not certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference directions do not follow from an observational acyclic ANM alone.
